questions.enonce_markdown:
The probability mass function of a discrete random variable $X$ is given by

$$
P(X = x) = \begin{cases} k(4 - x), & x = 1, 2, 3 \\ 0, & \text{elsewhere} \end{cases}
$$

Find the value of the constant $k$, *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The probabilities of a distribution sum to $1$:

$$
k(3) + k(2) + k(1) = 6k = 1 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad k = \frac{1}{6}.
$$

The distribution is therefore $P(X = 1) = \dfrac{1}{2}$, $P(X = 2) = \dfrac{1}{3}$, $P(X = 3) = \dfrac{1}{6}$.

$$
E(X) = \sum x\,P(X = x) = 1\cdot\frac{1}{2} + 2\cdot\frac{1}{3} + 3\cdot\frac{1}{6} = \frac{3 + 4 + 3}{6} = \frac{5}{3}.
$$

The mean of $X$ is $\dfrac{5}{3} \approx 1.67$.

First $E(X^2) = \sum x^2P(X = x) = 1\cdot\dfrac{1}{2} + 4\cdot\dfrac{1}{3} + 9\cdot\dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{3 + 8 + 9}{6} = \dfrac{10}{3}$.

$$
\operatorname{Var}(X) = E(X^2) - [E(X)]^2 = \frac{10}{3} - \frac{25}{9} = \frac{5}{9},
\qquad
\sigma = \sqrt{\frac{5}{9}} = \frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}.
$$

The standard deviation is $\dfrac{\sqrt{5}}{3} \approx 0.745$.

questions.enonce_markdown: The weights of components produced by a particular machine are normally distributed with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$. Given that $5\,\%$ of the components have weights greater than $85\ \mathrm{N}$ and $10\,\%$ have weights less than $25\ \mathrm{N}$, find, correct to $3$ significant figures, the values of $\mu$ and $\sigma$. *[9 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
Let $W$ be the weight, $W \sim N(\mu, \sigma^2)$, and $Z = \dfrac{W - \mu}{\sigma}$ the standardised variable.

$P(W > 85) = 0.05$, so $P(Z < z_1) = 0.95$ and, from the tables, $z_1 = 1.645$:

$$
\frac{85 - \mu}{\sigma} = 1.645.
$$

$P(W < 25) = 0.10$, so $P(Z < z_2) = 0.10$; by symmetry $z_2 = -1.282$:

$$
\frac{25 - \mu}{\sigma} = -1.282.
$$

That is, $\mu + 1.645\sigma = 85$ and $\mu - 1.282\sigma = 25$. Subtract the second from the first:

$$
2.927\,\sigma = 60 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad \sigma = 20.4988\ldots \approx 20.5.
$$

Substitute in the first equation: $\mu = 85 - 1.645 \times 20.4988 = 51.28\ldots \approx 51.3$.

Check with the second equation: $51.28 - 1.282 \times 20.4988 = 25.0$.

So $\mu \approx 51.3\ \mathrm{N}$ and $\sigma \approx 20.5\ \mathrm{N}$.
